findings.who: Married filing jointly; the spouse owns the royalty and had production taxes withheld from the spouse's royalty payments, while the taxpayer did not personally receive that royalty or have any tax taken out of the taxpayer's own payments.
findings.why_no: The gate says 'Did you pay' and 'your payments'; the taxpayer reads those words as limited to the taxpayer's own payments, not the spouse's.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 6, Line 4: 'Include taxes withheld by the producer on line 16.'
findings.fix: Ask 'Did you or your spouse pay costs for this royalty, or were any taken out of either spouse's payments?'

findings.who: A copyright, patent, or NIL royalty owner paid an accountant in 2025 for tax advice or return preparation allocable to the royalty, but paid no oil/gas production costs.
findings.why_no: The examples in the gate are production fees, severance/production taxes, and production costs; the filer does not read a general tax-preparation fee as a cost 'for this royalty' and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 6, Line 10: 'Include on line 10 fees for tax advice and the preparation of tax forms related to your rental real estate or royalty properties.'
findings.fix: Mention allocable tax advice and tax-preparation fees in the gate, or ask broadly about any expenses including professional and tax-preparation fees.

findings.who: A royalty owner paid an attorney in 2025 to defend title to the royalty or recover the royalty property; the fees are capitalizable rather than currently deductible.
findings.why_no: The filer reads 'costs' as deductible expenses; because the legal fees are capital, the filer answers no and never sees the help saying to capitalize them.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 6, Line 10: 'Do not deduct legal fees paid or incurred to defend or protect title to property, to recover property, or to develop or improve property. Instead, you must capitalize these fees and add them to the property’s basis.'
findings.fix: Ask whether any royalty-related legal or professional fees were paid or incurred, including capitalizable title/protection fees, and show the capitalization warning even when the gate is answered no.

findings.who: A mineral royalty owner paid state or local property (ad valorem) tax on the royalty interest, or had state income tax withheld from oil/gas royalties, but no severance or production tax.
findings.why_no: The gate lists only 'severance or production taxes'; the filer treats those as the only taxes asked about and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 6, General Instructions for Lines 5 Through 21: 'You can deduct all ordinary and necessary expenses, such as taxes'; and Line 4: 'even if state or local taxes were withheld from oil or gas payments you received. Include taxes withheld by the producer on line 16.'
findings.fix: Say 'taxes paid or withheld, including property, severance, production, or state/local taxes' rather than only severance or production taxes.

findings.who: A royalty owner paid an ordinary and necessary expense for the royalty in 2025, such as postage or office supplies used to manage the royalty, that is not a production cost or professional fee.
findings.why_no: The gate's parenthetical examples read as the whole category; the filer does not see an 'other' nonproduction expense as within 'costs for it' and answers no.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 7, Line 19: 'Enter on line 19 any ordinary and necessary expenses not listed on lines 5 through 18.'
findings.fix: Ask broadly about any ordinary and necessary expenses for the royalty, not only production fees/costs, and mention the line 19 catch-all.

locators: p. 6, General Instructions for Lines 5 Through 21
p. 7, Line 19, "Enter on line 19 any ordinary and necessary expenses not listed on lines 5 through 18"

findings.who: A filer whose royalty activity produced a loss in 2024 that Form 6198 disallowed because part of the investment was a nonrecourse loan. In 2025, this year's royalties less expenses come out slightly positive on line 21, before the carried-over loss is counted.
findings.why_no: The gate is computed as line 21 < $0 from this year's figures alone. If the prior-year disallowed loss is not part of line 21, the condition is false and the at-risk question is never asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 3, At-Risk Rules: 'In most cases, you must complete Form 6198 to figure your loss if you have: • A loss from an activity ... and • Amounts in the activity for which you are not at risk.' A loss disallowed in an earlier year stays a loss of the activity in later years.
findings.fix: Before computing the gate, ask whether any loss from this royalty was limited or disallowed in an earlier year (Form 6198 or Form 8582 carryover). Count that amount in the gate test, or open the gate whenever such a carryover exists.

findings.who: A filer who sold or abandoned a royalty interest in 2025 at a loss. The interest was bought with a nonrecourse note. Royalty income for the part of the year it was held makes line 21 zero or positive, and the disposition loss is reported on Form 4797 or Schedule D.
findings.why_no: The gate tests only line 21. The disposition loss never reaches line 21, so the at-risk question is not asked.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 3, At-Risk Rules: 'The at-risk rules in most cases limit the amount of loss (including loss on the disposition of assets) you can claim to the amount you could actually lose in the activity.'
findings.fix: Widen the gate: 'Line 21 is a loss, or you (or your spouse) sold, exchanged, abandoned, or otherwise disposed of all or part of this royalty property in 2025 at a loss.'

findings.who: A filer with positive line 21 whose amount at risk dropped below zero this year. For example, a recourse loan was converted to nonrecourse, or cash was withdrawn from the activity after losses had been deducted in earlier years.
findings.why_no: Line 21 is not a loss, so the gate is false. Under the at-risk rules, a negative amount at risk still requires Form 6198 and recapture of earlier deducted losses.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 3: 'use Form 6198 to figure your loss'; i1040se p. 7, Line 21: 'If you have amounts for which you are not at risk, use Form 6198 to determine the amount of your deductible loss.' The recapture itself comes from the Form 6198 instructions, which are not quoted here.
findings.fix: Ask whether any earlier-year loss from this royalty was deducted and the financing or the owner's investment changed this year (debt became nonrecourse, guarantee added, money withdrawn). Refuse on a yes.

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse co-owns the royalty interest and financed the spouse's share with a loan repayable only from the royalties, or a loan from the lessee.
findings.why_no: The question asks 'Was any money you put in borrowed without personal liability.' The filer answers for their own money only.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 3: 'Nonrecourse loans used to finance the activity, to acquire property used in the activity, or to acquire your interest in the activity ... are not at risk.'
findings.fix: Ask: 'Was any money you or your spouse put in ...'

findings.who: A filer who bought a royalty or mineral interest on seller financing: a note to the seller, secured only by the interest, with no personal liability. Or a filer who contributed property, not cash, that is protected by a stop-loss or buy-back agreement.
findings.why_no: The question says 'money you put in borrowed'. A seller-financed purchase does not feel like borrowing money, and contributed property is not 'money'. The help speaks of a 'loan', which the filer does not connect to an installment purchase.
findings.irs_text: i1040se p. 3: 'Nonrecourse loans used ... to acquire your interest in the activity' and 'Cash, property, or borrowed amounts used in the activity (or contributed to the activity, or used to acquire your interest in the activity) that are protected against loss by a guarantee, stop-loss agreement, or other similar arrangement.'
findings.fix: Reword: 'Did you or your spouse buy this royalty interest, or put money or property into it, using a loan or seller-financed note you are not personally liable to repay (including a note to the seller); or is any cash, property, or loan protected from loss by a guarantee, stop-loss, buy-back, or similar arrangement; or did any of it come from someone else with a stake in it, or a relative of theirs?'

locators: p. 3, At-Risk Rules, "In most cases, you must complete Form 6198 to figure your loss if you have"
p. 7, Line 21, "If you have amounts for which you are not at risk, use Form 6198 to determine the amount of your deductible loss"
